e-5703.knowledge_point: Calculating the Z-Score of a Given Observation
e-5703.problem: A data set has mean $\overline{x}=15$ and variance $\sigma^2=3.25$. Find the $z$-score of an observation $x=17.3,$ giving your answer to $2$ decimal places.
e-5703.worked_solution:
The $z$-score of an observation $x$ is defined by

$$
z = \frac{x-\overline{x}}{\sigma}.
$$

The $z$-score represents how many standard deviations an observation is above or below the mean of the data set.

Here, we're told that the mean is $\overline{x}=15,$ and we can calculate the standard deviation as

$$
\sigma = \sqrt{\sigma^2} = \sqrt{3.25}.
$$

So, the $z$-score of the observation $x=17.3$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}z & =\frac{x-\overset{―}{x}}{\sigma } \\  & ≈\frac{17.3-15}{\sqrt{3.25}} \\  & ≈1.28\end{aligned}
$$

to $2$ decimal places.

e-5705.knowledge_point: Finding the Value of an Observation, Standard Deviation, or Mean Given a Z-Score
e-5705.problem: A data set has a standard deviation $\sigma=1.2$ and an unknown mean. An observation of the data set has the value $x=13.2$ and $z$-score $z=-1.5.$ Find the mean of the data set.
e-5705.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overline{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x = \overline{x} + z \cdot \sigma
$$

Substituting $x=13.2,$ $z=-1.5,$ and $\sigma=1.2$ into the formula and solving for $\overline{x}$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\ 13.2 & =\overset{―}{x}+(-1.5)\cdot 1.2 \\ 13.2 & =\overset{―}{x}-1.8 \\ \overset{―}{x} & =13.2+1.8 \\ \overset{―}{x} & =15\end{aligned}
$$

e-8236.problem: A data set contains the observations $x_1=18, x_2=12$ with $z$-scores $z_1=2.8$ and $z_2=1.6,$ respectively. Find the mean of the data set.
e-8236.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overline{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x = \overline{x} + z \cdot \sigma
$$

From the first observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+2.8\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

From the second observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =\overset{¯}{x}+1.6\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting the second equation from the first and solving for $\sigma,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(18-12) & =(\overset{¯}{x}-\overset{¯}{x})+(2.8-1.6)\cdot \sigma  \\ 6 & =1.2\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this value back into our first equation and solving for $\bar{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+2.8\cdot \sigma  \\ 18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+2.8\cdot 5 \\ \overset{¯}{x} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8235.problem: The mean height of a group of basketball players is $178\textrm{ cm}$. A player in this group is $184\textrm{ cm}$ tall and his $z$-score is $z = 1.5$. Find the standard deviation of the basketball players' heights.
e-8235.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overline{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x = \overline{x} + z \cdot \sigma
$$

Substituting $x=184,$ $\overline{x}=178,$ and $z=1.5$ into the formula and solving for $\sigma,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\overset{―}{x}+z\cdot \sigma  \\ 184 & =178+1.5\cdot \sigma  \\ 6 & =1.5\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =\frac{6}{1.5} \\ \sigma  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the standard deviation of the players heights is $4\,\textrm{cm}.$
